note.text: Customs around meals vary between households and occasions. A careful comparison describes a particular setting and avoids claiming that everyone in a country behaves identically. Use in this household, whereas and both to express similarities and differences. Ask a host politely when unsure. Language practice can consider courtesy, permission and appreciation without ranking whole cultures or requiring a pupil to reveal family practices.

sections.heading: Apply the ideas locally
sections.text: Original comparison: In Bih's fictional household, guests wait until the host invites them to begin. At an imaginary club picnic, participants serve themselves when the organiser announces the meal. Both settings encourage considerate behaviour. The difference concerns the stated occasion; it does not prove that one community is polite and another is not.

sections.heading: Reason and check
sections.text: State the setting before comparing. Use both for a similarity and whereas for a contrast. Avoid unsupported words such as always and everyone. A polite question about a local practice is more useful than judging it from an unfamiliar rule.
